claims.text: An active-learning machine-learning interatomic potential augmented by ab initio reweighting can compute solid and liquid free energies with fidelity comparable to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The proposed framework can retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling effects.
The proposed framework will reduce computational cost by roughly a factor of 10 relative to TOR-TILD for elemental and binary systems.
A sparse ab initio dataset is sufficient to train the proposed potential for efficient thermodynamic integration.
Periodic ab initio benchmarking and reweighting can correct deviations of the machine-learning potential.
The intended temperature domain extends from approximately 100 K below to 100 K above the melting temperature.
High-fidelity local-environment descriptors capture the structural vibrations and anharmonic distortions that mediate solid–liquid free-energy differences.
Machine-learning-potential sampling explores thermodynamic configuration space more efficiently than explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
Active-learning ab initio corrections preserve subtle vibrational-entropy, anharmonic, and electron–vibration-coupling contributions to the free energy.
Faithful solid and liquid free energies will produce faithful fusion properties.
The proposed method will yield phase free energies within approximately 5 meV/atom of full ab initio molecular-dynamics results.
The proposed method will predict melting temperatures within approximately 10 K of full ab initio molecular-dynamics results.
The proposed method will provide latent heat as a derived fusion property.
The proposed performance and fidelity claims are restricted to elemental metals and binary alloys.
Comparable speedups and fidelity are not guaranteed for multicomponent high-entropy systems without additional development.
Prior machine-learning-potential work on elemental and binary systems supports the proposed method.
